entities.summary:
Kapila, also referred to as Cakradhanus, is a Vedic sage in Hindu tradition, regarded as the founder of the Samkhya school of Hindu philosophy.

Born in ancient India, Kapila's teachings flourished during the 8th century BCE, contributing significantly to the development of Hindu thought.

The core of Kapila's philosophy lies in the concept of the dualistic nature of reality, which posits that the universe is composed of two fundamental principles: purusha (the unchanging, eternal Self) and prakriti (the changing, material world).

This dichotomy is central to the Samkhya system, which emphasizes the attainment of liberation through the realization of the individual's true nature.

Kapila's teachings had a profound impact on the evolution of Hindu philosophy, influencing the development of Yoga, Vedanta, and other schools of thought.

A striking example of the enduring legacy of Kapila's philosophy is the continued relevance of the Samkhya system in modern Hindu spiritual practices, demonstrating the lasting influence of this ancient sage.
